lines.say: A query travels through more parts of PostgreSQL than you think.
lines.cap: A query travels through *more* *parts* than you think.

lines.say: This is episode three of the PostgreSQL DBA series. Today: the processes, memory and files behind every query.
lines.cap: Episode 3: the *processes,* *memory* and *files* behind a query.

lines.say: PostgreSQL uses a client server model. Your app, or psql, is the client.
lines.cap: *Client/server* model: your app or *psql* is the *client.*

lines.say: The server is a program called postgres. Client and server can run on different machines.
lines.cap: The server program is *postgres.* It can be on *another* *host.*

lines.say: The first process to start is the postmaster. It listens on a port and waits for connections.
lines.cap: The *postmaster* starts first and *listens* for connections.

lines.say: Every time a client connects, the postmaster starts a new backend process just for that connection.
lines.cap: Each connection gets its *own* *backend* *process.*

lines.say: From then on, your client talks only to its backend, which parses your query, plans it, runs it, and sends the rows back.
lines.cap: The backend *parses,* *plans,* *executes* and returns rows.

lines.say: Backends don't work alone. They all use one common memory area called shared memory.
lines.cap: All backends use one common *shared* *memory* area.

lines.say: Its largest part is shared buffers, a cache of data pages, usually eight kilobytes each.
lines.cap: Largest part: *shared_buffers,* a cache of *8 kB* pages.

lines.say: When a backend changes a page in memory, that page is called dirty, until it is written back to disk.
lines.cap: A changed page is *dirty* until written back to disk.

lines.say: But first, the change is logged. Changes reach the data files only after their WAL records are flushed to permanent storage.
lines.cap: *WAL* first: data files change only *after* WAL is flushed.

lines.say: That is the write ahead log. After a crash, PostgreSQL can redo the missing changes from the WAL.
lines.cap: After a crash, changes are *redone* from the *WAL.*

lines.say: Now the helpers. The background writer writes dirty pages to disk a little at a time.
lines.cap: *Background* *writer:* writes dirty pages, a little at a time.

lines.say: The checkpointer runs checkpoints. The WAL writer writes WAL records from shared memory to the WAL files.
lines.cap: *Checkpointer* runs checkpoints. *WAL* *writer* writes WAL files.

lines.say: The autovacuum launcher starts workers that vacuum and analyze your tables.
lines.cap: *Autovacuum* *launcher* starts workers to *vacuum* and *analyze.*

lines.say: And background workers run extra code, for features like parallel queries and logical replication.
lines.cap: *Background* *workers:* parallel queries, logical replication.

lines.say: On disk, the cluster lives in the data directory. Table and index files sit under base, and WAL files under pg_wal.
lines.cap: *Data* *directory:* tables under *base,* WAL under *pg_wal.*

lines.say: Let's see it live. In psql, select backend type from pg_stat_activity.
lines.cap: Live: *backend_type* from *pg_stat_activity.*

lines.say: On PostgreSQL sixteen we get six rows. One is a client backend: that's us.
lines.cap: PostgreSQL 16: *6* *rows,* one *client* *backend* is us.

lines.say: The list depends on version and settings. PostgreSQL eighteen, for example, uses I/O workers by default.
lines.cap: The list *varies:* PostgreSQL 18 adds *I/O* *workers* by default.

lines.say: A common misconception: one PostgreSQL server means one process. In reality, every connection gets its own backend process.
lines.cap: Myth: *one* *server,* *one* *process.* Reality: one per *connection.*

lines.say: DBA takeaway: every connection is a whole process, so a common practice is a connection pooler like PgBouncer.
lines.cap: Each connection is a *process.* Common practice: a *pooler.*

lines.say: Recap: the postmaster, one backend per connection, shared buffers, WAL first, and background helpers.
lines.cap: Recap: *postmaster,* *backends,* *shared* *buffers,* *WAL,* *helpers.*

lines.say: Next up: what happens when you run a SELECT. Follow so you don't miss it, and send this to a friend who's learning PostgreSQL.
lines.cap: Next up: life of a *SELECT.* *Follow* and share.

scenes.text: It depends on version and settings. PostgreSQL 18 defaults to io_method = worker, with 3 I/O workers.

scenes.text: PostgreSQL is process per connection: every client gets its own backend process.

scenes.title: Connections are not free
scenes.text: Each connection is a whole backend process. A common practice: a connection pooler such as PgBouncer.
